sourceAgencies: Glen Rock Borough Council & Glen Rock BOE Collective Bargaining Agreements
Bergen Municipal Employee Benefits Fund (BMED / JIF)
NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (SHBP / SEHBP)

overview.percentageOfCombinedBudgets: 18.8% of all public spending in Glen Rock Borough goes directly to employee health insurance and pensions

healthcarePlans.providers: Bergen Municipal JIF Direct Access (BMED) & School Employees' Health Benefits Program (SEHBP)

primaryPlans.description: In-network copay model replacing state SHBP coverage with predictable negotiated dental and prescription formularies to protect borough taxpayers from state premium spikes.

primaryPlans.planName: NJ Educators Health Plan (NJEHP / Chapter 44) & Garden State Plan
primaryPlans.description: School district plan option for certified teachers and school staff, capping employee contributions to a salary-indexed percentage (1.7% to 7.2%).

primaryPlans.planName: Prescription Drug Card (BMED / Express Scripts Formulary)
primaryPlans.description: Retail, mail-order, and specialty biologics with taxpayers subsidizing over 85% of total pharmacy costs.
Preventive, restorative, and orthodontic dental coverage plus optical exams for eligible municipal and school staff.

rules.tier: Borough Municipal Staff & Police (Chapter 78 Tier 4 Grid)
rules.employeeContribution: 10% to 35% of premium based on salary tier
rules.taxpayerContribution: 65% to 90% of total family premium ($24,000 - $31,000/yr subsidy)
rules.note: For a police officer or DPW worker with a $35,000 family health plan, Glen Rock taxpayers subsidize ~$24,500+ every year.

rules.tier: Glen Rock BOE Teachers & School Staff (Chapter 44 NJEHP)
rules.note: Because employee contributions are tied to salary rather than premium cost, annual health insurance rate hikes fall directly on the Glen Rock school property tax levy.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Multi-million dollar ongoing retiree health expenditure
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Employees retiring with 25+ years of credited pensionable service receive employer-paid health coverage until Medicare eligibility, plus Medicare Part B reimbursement.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.legalAuthority: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (N.J.S.A. 43:16A & 43:15A)
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Mandatory employer contributions to Police & Firemen's Retirement System (PFRS) for Glen Rock police officers and Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) for civilian borough employees. School district educators participate in Teachers' Pension and Annuity Fund (TPAF).

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.benefitName: Accumulated Sick Leave & Terminal Leave Payouts
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Capped at $15,000 for post-2010 hires; legacy liabilities for veteran staff
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Under N.J.S.A. 11A:6-19.2, terminal sick payouts are capped at $15,000 for personnel hired after May 2010. Grandfathered veteran staff retain contractually accumulated bank time cash-outs.
